plan: [I will bid my true private value, $48. In a third-price (k=3) auction with no prior history and iid uniform values, the payment if I win equals the second-highest of the four opponents and is independent of my own bid. Bidding my value maximizes my expected surplus without risking overbidding above my value (which could create negative payoff if the third price exceeds my value). [Assume opponents use monotone linear bids b(x)=c·x. If I bid B, win probability = (B/(49c))^4 and conditional payment = 0.4·B (the second-highest of 4 opponents mapped by c cancels). Expected payoff U(B)=k·B^4·(v-0.4B), maximized at B=2v. Symmetric equilibrium gives c=2, so optimal bid = 2v. With my value v=$38, bid = $76 to maximize long-run expected profit.]

For symmetric IPV uniform draws, the equilibrium is linear shading with factor (n-m+1)/(n-1) where n=5, m=3 → factor = 3/4. Shade my bid to 0.75×value to maximize expected surplus. [Third-price auction with 5 bidders: if I win I pay the second-highest of the other four, independent of my own bid. For uniform values the symmetric equilibrium is b(v) = (n-1)/(n-k+1) * v = 4/3 * v for n=5, k=3. With my value v=15, bid 20 maximizes expected long-run profit.]
